title: add_episode is impractically slow for >5KB content — proposal: skip_extraction parameter
body:
## Summary

`Graphiti.add_episode()` issues *N₁ + N_entities + N_edges + N_dedup* serial LLM calls per episode. On a rate-limited LLM endpoint (concurrency-capped Aliyun qwen3.6-plus, where each call costs 8-30s and `max_coroutines` must be set to 1 to avoid HTTP 429), this translates to:

| Episode body | Measured / projected wall time |
|---|---|
| 1 sentence (3 entities) | ~626 s (measured) |
| 5 KB markdown (~30 entities, ~50 edges) | ~30-50 min (projected from partial run) |
| **49 KB markdown** | **~5-10 hr (projected)** |

This makes ingesting **canonical documents** (READMEs, design docs, RFCs, ADRs) via `add_episode` impractical, even though the content is exactly the kind of pre-curated material a graph wants.

## Environment

| Component | Setting |
|---|---|
| graphiti-core | latest |
| Graph backend | FalkorDB 8.x (Docker) |
| LLM client | `AnthropicClient` (Aliyun-compatible) |
| LLM model | `qwen3.6-plus` |
| Embedder | `FastembedEmbedder` (local, `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`) |
| `max_coroutines` | **1** (required for this LLM endpoint) |
| Per-LLM-call latency | 8-30 s (measured, all HTTP 200) |
| Entity / edge schema | 13 entity types, 13 edge types |

## Diagnostic notes

- It is **not** an LLM rate-limit issue — all calls return 200; no 429.
- It is **not** a FastEmbed / onnxruntime deadlock — 10 sequential embeddings take 1 s; 10 parallel take 0.1 s. ONNX worker threads in `WorkerData::SetBlocked` are *idle workers waiting for work*, not deadlocked.
- It is **not** a TCP / network issue — connection to LLM endpoint is intermittent only because each request opens and closes its own connection.
- It **is** call multiplicity × serialization. For a 5 KB doc that produces ~30 entities and ~50 edges, graphiti issues 30 (dedup) + 30 (attribute extraction) + 100 (edge fact + classify) ≈ 160 LLM calls. At 10 s/call × `max_coroutines=1` = **~27 min minimum, serialized**.

## Proposal: opt-in `skip_extraction` parameter

For use cases where the caller wants to register **pre-curated knowledge** (canonical docs / capsules / RFCs) as Episodic nodes *without* paying for LLM extraction:

```python
await g.add_episode(
    ...,
    skip_extraction=True,
)
```

When `True`:
- Build the `EpisodicNode` from `name / episode_body / source_description / reference_time` as today
- Skip `extract_nodes`, `resolve_extracted_nodes`, `_extract_and_resolve_edges`, `extract_attributes_from_nodes`
- Call `_process_episode_data` with `nodes=[]` and `entity_edges=[]` to persist the Episodic node
- Return `AddEpisodeResults` with empty nodes/edges

Patch attached (93-line unified diff): https://github.com/commiao/kg-hub/blob/main/docs/patches/graphiti-skip-extraction.patch

**Measured speedup** on the same 5 KB body: 30+ min (full extraction) → **0.03 s** (`skip_extraction=True`). That's >50,000×, because the LLM critical path is gone entirely.

The Episodic node remains queryable via FalkorDB `db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes('Episodic', ...)` (i.e., `kg_episode_search`-style consumers). Entities/edges from the doc can be opted into later via re-ingestion when the user has reason to want graph navigation over that content.

## Other fix candidates (mentioned for completeness)

1. **Docs**: Add a throughput-expectation note to README (`add_episode` issues N×(entities+edges) LLM calls; cap throughput planning at 1 entity + 1 edge per second / `max_coroutines`).
2. **Parallel entity ops**: Within a single episode, attribute extraction across entities can run in parallel; dedup-by-name can be a single batched query.
3. **Entity cap**: A `max_entities_per_episode` parameter would bound worst-case latency.

I'm happy to file a focused PR for **P1 (`skip_extraction`)** — it's the smallest surface change with the highest practical payoff for users on rate-limited endpoints.

## Reference

Full diagnostic + downstream context (kg-hub project):
- Bug report: https://github.com/commiao/kg-hub/blob/main/docs/BUG-add-episode-throughput.md
- Patch: https://github.com/commiao/kg-hub/blob/main/docs/patches/graphiti-skip-extraction.patch
- README: https://github.com/commiao/kg-hub/blob/main/README.md

title: FalkorDriver.default_group_id ('\_') is rejected by validate_group_id
body:
## Summary

In `graphiti-core==0.29.1`, `FalkorDriver.default_group_id` is set to the literal two-character string `\_` (backslash + underscore), but `graphiti_core.helpers.validate_group_id` only allows `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`. Any call that flows the driver's default into the validator (e.g. `add_episode` / `search` without an explicit `group_id`) raises `GroupIdValidationError`, so the FalkorDB driver is effectively unusable out of the box without supplying `group_id` at every call site.

## Versions

- `graphiti-core` 0.29.1
- Python 3.12
- FalkorDB backend

## Where the conflict lives

`graphiti_core/driver/falkordb_driver.py` (line 112):

```python
class FalkorDriver(GraphDriver):
    provider = GraphProvider.FALKORDB
    default_group_id: str = '\\_'
```

`graphiti_core/helpers.py` (validate_group_id, ~line 156):

```python
if not re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$', group_id):
    raise GroupIdValidationError(group_id)
```

The backslash in `\_` is not in the allowed character class, so the validator rejects the driver's own default.

## Minimal repro

```python
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime
from graphiti_core import Graphiti
from graphiti_core.driver.falkordb_driver import FalkorDriver
from graphiti_core.nodes import EpisodeType
# ... construct llm_client + embedder ...

async def main():
    g = Graphiti(
        graph_driver=FalkorDriver(host="localhost", port=6379),
        llm_client=...,
        embedder=...,
    )
    await g.add_episode(
        name="t",
        episode_body="x",
        source=EpisodeType.text,
        source_description="t",
        reference_time=datetime.now(),
    )

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Observed behavior

```
graphiti_core.errors.GroupIdValidationError: group_id "\_" must contain only alphanumeric characters, dashes, or underscores
```

## Expected behavior

`add_episode` / `search` with no explicit `group_id` should succeed against `FalkorDriver` using whatever default the driver advertises, without the caller having to know that the driver's default happens to be rejected by the shared validator.

## Workaround

Pass an explicit `group_id` (e.g. `group_id="default"`) on every `add_episode` / `search` call. This sidesteps the driver default entirely.

## Notes

Not proposing a patch — the fix is a maintainer call between (a) widening `validate_group_id` to accept whatever character class FalkorDB needs in the underlying database name, (b) changing `FalkorDriver.default_group_id` to a value the validator already accepts, or (c) renaming `default_group_id` so the per-driver "internal default DB name" is decoupled from the user-facing `group_id` that the validator gates. Each has different blast radius for existing FalkorDB deployments and for the cross-driver contract, so I'd rather flag the inconsistency than pick one.

title: FalkorDB driver factory drops URI username, breaks FalkorDB Cloud auth
body:
# Bug: FalkorDB driver factory drops the URI's `username`, breaks FalkorDB Cloud auth

**Repo:** `getzep/graphiti`
**File:** `mcp_server/src/services/factories.py` (URI parsing) +
`mcp_server/src/graphiti_mcp_server.py` (FalkorDriver instantiation)
**Tag/commit:** observed on current `main` (cloned 2026-05-31).

## What happens

Following the MCP server quickstart with a **FalkorDB Cloud** instance, the
server fails to start with:

```
graphiti_mcp_server - ERROR - Failed to initialize Graphiti client:
  invalid username-password pair or user is disabled.
...
redis.exceptions.AuthenticationError: invalid username-password pair or
user is disabled.
```

even when `FALKORDB_URI` and `FALKORDB_PASSWORD` are set correctly and the
password matches what's embedded in the URI.

## Root cause

FalkorDB Cloud-provisioned instances expose a URI of the form

```
redis://falkordb:<password>@<host>.cloud:<port>
```

(`falkordb`, not the implicit Redis `default`, is the AUTH user — and the
`default` user is disabled on those instances).

`src/services/factories.py` parses the URI for host + port only and **discards
`parsed.username`**:

```python
parsed = urlparse(uri)
host = parsed.hostname or 'localhost'
port = parsed.port or 6379

return {
    'driver': 'falkordb',
    'host': host,
    'port': port,
    'password': password,
    'database': falkor_config.database,
}
```

`src/graphiti_mcp_server.py` then constructs `FalkorDriver(host=…, port=…,
password=…, database=…)` — no `username`. The driver in turn calls
`FalkorDB(host, port, username=None, password=…)`, so the Redis client
attempts AUTH as the implicit `default` user, which the FalkorDB Cloud
instance does not have / has disabled → `AuthenticationError`.

Note: `FalkorDriver.__init__` *does* accept a `username` kwarg
(`graphiti_core/driver/falkordb_driver.py:__init__`), it's just never
populated from the URI by the MCP server's factory layer.

## Suggested fix

1. In `mcp_server/src/services/factories.py`, capture the URI's `username`
   (and optionally accept a `FALKORDB_USERNAME` env override for symmetry with
   `FALKORDB_URI` / `FALKORDB_PASSWORD`):

   ```python
   parsed = urlparse(uri)
   host = parsed.hostname or 'localhost'
   port = parsed.port or 6379
   username = os.environ.get('FALKORDB_USERNAME') or parsed.username

   return {
       'driver': 'falkordb',
       'host': host,
       'port': port,
       'username': username,
       'password': password,
       'database': falkor_config.database,
   }
   ```

2. In `mcp_server/src/graphiti_mcp_server.py`, pass `username` through to the
   driver:

   ```python
   falkor_driver = FalkorDriver(
       host=db_config['host'],
       port=db_config['port'],
       username=db_config.get('username'),
       password=db_config['password'],
       database=db_config['database'],
   )
   ```

Applied locally as a 2-file diff (≈4 lines added), the MCP server connects to
FalkorDB Cloud cleanly with the same `FALKORDB_URI` / `FALKORDB_PASSWORD` env
vars the docs already prescribe.

## Reproduction

1. Provision a FalkorDB Cloud free-tier instance (https://cloud.falkordb.com).
   The provisioned URI looks like `redis://falkordb:<pwd>@…:<port>`.
2. Configure the MCP server per the quickstart, with
   `FALKORDB_URI=<that-uri>` and `FALKORDB_PASSWORD=<that-pwd>`.
3. Start the MCP server → it fails with the `AuthenticationError` above.

## Environment

- macOS 14 (Sonoma), arm64
- Python 3.10 (uv-managed venv per `mcp_server/`)
- `graphiti_core` from `mcp_server/.venv` — `falkordb_driver.py` confirmed to
  accept the `username` kwarg.
- FalkorDB Cloud, ap-south-1 region.

title: [BUG] FalkorDB: NUL byte (\x00) in a string property fails the whole query with "Failed to parse query parameter '<name>' value"
body:
### Summary

When any string value passed as a FalkorDB query parameter contains a NUL byte (`\x00`), FalkorDB rejects the **entire** query with:

```
Failed to parse query parameter '<name>' value
```

Because this happens at save time (e.g. the bulk Episodic save `UNWIND $episodes ... SET n.content = episode.content`), affected episodes are **silently dropped** from ingest — the error is per-episode and the run continues, so it's easy to miss.

### Environment
- `graphiti-core` 0.29.1, FalkorDB backend (`graphiti-core[falkordb]`), `falkordb` client 1.2.0.

### Root cause
FalkorDB query parameters are serialized into a `CYPHER <key>=<value> ...` header by the client. `falkordb/helpers.py::quote_string` escapes only backslash and double-quote:

```python
v = v.replace("\\", "\\\\")
v = v.replace('"', '\\"')
```

It does **not** handle `\x00`. A NUL embedded in a string value is emitted verbatim into the params header, and FalkorDB's parser fails on it. (Plain newlines/tabs are fine — only NUL trips it, which is why it shows up rarely.)

### How we hit it
Text extracted from PPTX/PDF source documents frequently contains stray NUL bytes (e.g. between glyphs). 12 of our ~2,000 episodes — all from board-meeting decks — failed ingest. Bisecting one failing episode's `content` pinpointed a single `\x00` at byte 864 (`"...Seamless Recruiting \x00 Onboarding..."`).

### Minimal reproduction
```python
g.query(
    "UNWIND $episodes AS e MERGE (n:Episodic {uuid:e.uuid}) SET n.content=e.content RETURN n.uuid",
    {"episodes": [{"uuid": "t", "content": "a \x00 b"}]},
)
# -> redis.exceptions.ResponseError: Failed to parse query parameter 'episodes' value
# Stripping the \x00 -> succeeds.
```

### Impact
Silent data loss during ingest for any content (commonly PPTX/PDF-extracted) containing NUL bytes.

### Suggested fix
NUL can never be stored in a FalkorDB string property, so it's safe to strip it. Either:
1. **graphiti-core (FalkorDB driver):** recursively strip `\x00` from string params in `FalkorDriver.execute_query` / `FalkorDriverSession.run` before sending (one-liner-ish, no behavior change for valid data), or
2. **falkordb-py:** have `quote_string` strip/reject NUL.

Happy to send a PR for option 1 if useful. (Distinct from the edge re-match perf issue #1272.)

title: to_prompt_json crashes on datetime attribute values (Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable)
body:
### What I was doing

Ingesting episodes with custom entity types whose attributes include `datetime`/`date` fields (a date extracted into an entity attribute, e.g. a contract `signed_at` or a person `date_of_birth`). The **first** ingest of a brand-new entity succeeds. The **second** ingest that touches the same entity triggers entity-summary regeneration, which serializes the entity's `attributes` dict into the summary prompt and crashes.

### Call path

```
extract_attributes_from_nodes
  → _extract_entity_summaries_batch
  → extract_summaries_batch
  → to_prompt_json(context['attributes'])
  → json.dumps(...)   # graphiti_core/prompts/prompt_helpers.py — no default= handler
```

### Expected

`to_prompt_json` serializes attribute dicts containing `datetime`/`date` values (rendering them as ISO-8601), the way attribute data realistically looks.

### Actual

```
TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable
```

`graphiti_core/prompts/prompt_helpers.py::to_prompt_json` calls `json.dumps(data, ...)` with no `default=` handler, so any `datetime`/`date` value raises.

### Minimal repro

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from graphiti_core.prompts.prompt_helpers import to_prompt_json

to_prompt_json({"signed_at": datetime(2024, 3, 15, tzinfo=timezone.utc)})
# TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable
```

### Version

graphiti-core 0.29.x (also present on `main` / v0.29.1).

### Fix

PR incoming — adds a `default=` fallback to `to_prompt_json` (ISO-8601 for `date`/`datetime`, `str()` otherwise) plus unit tests. Output is unchanged for already-serializable data.

title: [Bug]: NeptuneDriver connects/builds indices but Graphiti.add_episode fails on Neptune + AOSS
body:
### What happened?

`graphiti-core==0.29.1` can construct a `NeptuneDriver`, run a signed raw
Neptune query, and build AOSS indices, but `Graphiti.add_episode(...)` fails
on the Neptune + AOSS backend.

This looks like a driver-contract bug in `NeptuneDriver`, not a connectivity
or IAM issue. Raw `execute_query("RETURN 1 AS one")` works, and
`build_indices_and_constraints()` reaches AOSS.

### Environment

- graphiti-core: 0.29.1
- Python: 3.13
- Graph backend: Amazon Neptune Database
- Search backend for NeptuneDriver: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (AOSS)
- Auth: AWS SigV4 through boto3 credentials

### Version check

- Latest stable PyPI release checked before filing: `graphiti-core==0.29.1`
- Reproduced on: `graphiti-core==0.29.1`
- I have not claimed reproduction on `main` unless maintainers want me to test
  a source install.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
import asyncio
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from graphiti_core import Graphiti
from graphiti_core.driver.neptune_driver import NeptuneDriver
from graphiti_core.nodes import EpisodeType


async def main():
    driver = NeptuneDriver(
        host="neptune-db://<neptune-cluster-endpoint>",
        port=8182,
        aoss_host="<aoss-endpoint>",
        aoss_port=443,
    )

    graphiti = Graphiti(graph_driver=driver)

    # These work in the same environment.
    await graphiti.build_indices_and_constraints()
    rows, _, _ = await driver.execute_query("RETURN 1 AS one")
    assert rows[0]["one"] == 1

    # This fails.
    await graphiti.add_episode(
        name="neptune-repro",
        episode_body="Alice likes chess.",
        source=EpisodeType.text,
        source_description="repro",
        reference_time=datetime.now(UTC),
        group_id="repro-group",
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Actual behavior

With `group_id`:

```text
AttributeError: 'NeptuneDriver' object has no attribute '_database'
```

<details>
<summary>Traceback for the first failure</summary>

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../graphiti_core/graphiti.py", line 1079, in add_episode
    if group_id != self.driver._database:
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NeptuneDriver' object has no attribute '_database'
```

</details>

After locally setting `_database`, or on paths that reach entity/community
similarity search, Neptune receives nested params and openCypher parameters
are unbound:

```text
MalformedQueryException: MissingParameter
```

Later in the same ingestion path, AOSS Serverless rejects custom document IDs
when `save_to_aoss()` sends `_id = d["uuid"]` in bulk actions:

```text
Document ID is not supported
```

### Expected behavior

`Graphiti.add_episode(...)` should work with `NeptuneDriver` the same way it
works with the other supported graph drivers:

- group-scoped ingestion should not crash on `_database`
- query params passed as `params={...}` should be flattened before being sent
  to Neptune
- AOSS writes should use auto-generated `_id` and store the logical UUID in
  source fields
- add/search/delete should be testable against Neptune + AOSS

### Suspected code points

- `graphiti_core/graphiti.py`: `add_episode()` expects `self.driver._database`
  and calls `self.driver.clone(database=group_id)`.
- `graphiti_core/driver/neptune_driver.py`: `NeptuneDriver.__init__` does not
  set `_database`.
- `graphiti_core/driver/driver.py`: base `clone()` returns `self`.
- `graphiti_core/search/search_utils.py`: Neptune search path calls
  `driver.execute_query(query, params=filter_params, search_vector=..., ...)`.
- `graphiti_core/driver/neptune_driver.py`: `execute_query()` wraps all kwargs
  into params, causing `{"params": {...}}` nesting.
- `graphiti_core/driver/neptune_driver.py`: `save_to_aoss()` includes custom
  `_id`, which AOSS Serverless rejects.

### Suggested fix direction

1. Resolve the Neptune `group_id` / database semantics first. This appears to
   be the main design decision:
   - Should `NeptuneDriver` emulate database-style group switching with
     `_database` + `clone(database=...)`, similar to the other drivers?
   - Or should Neptune keep `group_id` as a property-level namespace only,
     with no database switch?

   This choice determines what `_database` should mean for Neptune and how
   `clone(database=...)` should behave.

2. Fix explicit query parameter forwarding in `NeptuneDriver.execute_query()`
   so `params={...}` is not nested under a literal `params` key:

```python
params = dict(kwargs.pop("params", {}) or {})
params.update(kwargs)
params.pop("routing_", None)
```

`routing_` is passed by the shared search code for routing-aware drivers, but
Neptune does not appear to use it; `KuzuDriver` already strips `routing_` for a
similar reason. A PR should also verify whether Neptune accepts extra
parameters such as `search_vector`, `limit`, or `min_score` when the query does
not reference them. If not, the driver should strip or only forward the params
used by the query.

3. Change `save_to_aoss()` to avoid custom `_id`; keep `uuid` in the indexed
   source fields. Also audit any update/delete path that assumed
   `_id == uuid`; those paths need to find documents by the source `uuid`
   field before updating/deleting.
4. Add a NeptuneDriver contract test that exercises:
   - `Graphiti.add_episode()`
   - group_id path
   - parameterized similarity-search path
   - AOSS Serverless-compatible bulk action shape

### Additional notes

The public docs show both the `add_episode` API and the NeptuneDriver
construction path, but the issue appears only when the full ingestion path is
run against Neptune + AOSS. A connectivity-only smoke test is not sufficient
to catch it.

title: docs(mcp_server): Ollama config example uses outdated flat provider schema + sentence_transformers embedder
body:
### Summary

The **Ollama** configuration example in `mcp_server/README.md` (the "Using Ollama" section) uses an outdated/inconsistent config layout compared to the rest of the document.

### Details

The Ollama example currently reads:

```yaml
llm:
  provider: "openai"
  model: "gpt-oss:120b"
  api_base: "http://localhost:11434/v1"
  api_key: "ollama"  # dummy key required

embedder:
  provider: "sentence_transformers"  # recommended for local setup
  model: "all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
```

Two problems:

1. **Inconsistent provider schema.** Every other config block in the same README (the LLM `openai`/`anthropic`/etc. and database `falkordb`/`neo4j` sections) uses the nested `providers:` form with `api_url`, e.g.:

   ```yaml
   provider: "falkordb"
   providers:
     falkordb:
       ...
   ```

   The Ollama example is the only one still using the flat top-level `api_base` / `api_key` keys, which don't match the nested schema the rest of the docs (and config loader) expect.

2. **Embedder.** The example points the embedder at `sentence_transformers`, which requires a separate local model/dependency. Since Ollama already exposes an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint on the same port, the example can stay self-contained by using the `openai` embedder provider against the Ollama URL.

### Suggested fix

```yaml
llm:
  provider: "openai"
  model: "gpt-oss:120b"  # or your preferred Ollama model
  providers:
    openai:
      api_key: "ollama"  # dummy key required
      api_url: "http://localhost:11434/v1"

embedder:
  provider: "openai"  # Ollama serves embeddings on the same OpenAI-compatible API
  model: "nomic-embed-text"  # or another Ollama embedding model
  dimensions: 768  # set to match your embedding model
  providers:
    openai:
      api_key: "ollama"
      api_url: "http://localhost:11434/v1"
```

### Note for maintainers

This exact change was proposed in PR #1514, but I'm closing that PR because the repo's `CLAAssistant` workflow is currently failing on the maintainer side with `graphql call to get committers details failed: HttpError: Bad credentials` — so the CLA check can't go green regardless of who signs. The one-file doc change above can be applied directly. Worth checking the CLA action's token while you're at it.

title: MCP server: queue worker silently garbage-collected under streamable-http — add_memory queues but never processes
body:
# Issue: Queue worker silently garbage-collected under streamable-http transport — `add_memory` queues but never processes

## Summary

`add_memory` returns `"Episode 'X' queued for processing"` (200 OK) but the queue worker never starts processing under the **streamable-http transport**. No LLM calls happen, no episodes appear in the graph database, no error logs are produced. `search_nodes`, `get_episodes` and other read tools work correctly because they read pre-existing data.

Root cause: `services/queue_service.py:add_episode_task()` calls `asyncio.create_task(...)` without keeping a reference to the returned task. Per Python asyncio documentation:

> *"Save a reference to the result of this function, to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution. The event loop only keeps **weak references** to tasks. A task that isn't referenced elsewhere may be garbage collected at any time, even before it's done."*
> — [docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task)

Under streamable-http transport, GC pressure during request handling is high enough that the orphaned worker task gets collected before its first `await` on the queue completes.

## Reproduction

> Re-verified against `main` on 2026-06-11: `services/queue_service.py` still discards the `asyncio.create_task` result (only a `_queue_workers: dict[str, bool]` flag is kept).

**Environment:**
- `zepai/knowledge-graph-mcp:1.0.2-standalone` (graphiti-core 0.28.2, mcp 1.26.0)
- Transport: `streamable-http`
- Backend: FalkorDB (also reproducible with Neo4j per fork reports)
- LLM gateway: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- Kubernetes Deployment, single replica, 256Mi memory limit

**Steps:**
1. Start MCP server with `transport: http` (streamable-http)
2. Connect MCP client (e.g., `curl` or Claude Code via mcp-remote)
3. Send `tools/call` for `add_memory` with valid `name` + `episode_body`
4. Observe response: `"Episode '<name>' queued for processing"` (success, 200 OK)
5. Wait 60 seconds and observe pod logs

**Expected:**
- `INFO services.queue_service - Starting episode queue worker for group_id: <gid>`
- `INFO services.queue_service - Processing episode <uuid> for group <gid>`
- HTTP requests to LLM/embedder
- `INFO graphiti_core.graphiti - Completed add_episode in N ms`
- New `Episodic` node in graph database

**Actual:**
- No log output between request and a hypothetical 60-minute mark
- No HTTP requests to LLM/embedder
- No new `Episodic` node in graph database
- No error in logs (silent failure)

## Diagnosis

The worker task created at `queue_service.py:45`:

```python
if not self._queue_workers.get(group_id, False):
    asyncio.create_task(self._process_episode_queue(group_id))  # ← result discarded
```

…is discarded. asyncio's event loop only keeps **weak** references to tasks. Under streamable-http transport, when a request handler completes and triggers garbage collection, the orphaned task is collected before its first `await` on the empty queue can suspend it.

Verification: we instrumented the running pod by replacing `queue_service.py` with a patched version that stores the task reference in `self._worker_tasks`. After the patch:

```
12:45:09 - Starting episode queue worker for group_id: kiroot_v2
12:45:09 - Processing episode None for group kiroot_v2
12:45:13 - HTTP Request: POST .../v1/responses "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
12:45:14 - HTTP Request: POST .../v1/embeddings "HTTP/1.1 200 OK" (×6)
12:46:01 - Completed add_episode in 51522.60 ms
12:46:01 - Successfully processed episode None for group kiroot_v2
```

FalkorDB Episodic count went from 569 → 570 with the test episode `"GC-Anchor-Patch Verification 2026-05-10"`.

## Proposed fix

A 6-line, behaviorally-neutral change to `services/queue_service.py`: store the worker task reference in a dict so it's strongly held until it exits.

A PR with the 6-line fix follows.

## References

- [asyncio.create_task documentation warning](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task)
- Related FastMCP issue with similar root cause (different framework but same anti-pattern): [PrefectHQ/fastmcp#1115](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/issues/1115)
- Several community forks worked around this by switching to Redis-backed persistent queues:
  - [michabbb/graphiti-mcp-but-working](https://github.com/michabbb/graphiti-mcp-but-working) — BRPOPLPUSH pattern
  - [itcook/graphiti-mcp-pro](https://github.com/itcook/graphiti-mcp-pro) — async parallel processing rewrite

The fix proposed here is much smaller (6 lines) and preserves the existing architecture while eliminating the GC race.

title: PR Triage workflow fails on all fork PRs with internal directory mismatch in claude-code-action
body:
## Summary

The **PR Triage** workflow (`PR Triage` / `.github/workflows/triage.yml`) fails on every fork PR with an internal error in the `anthropics/claude-code-action` runner. This is not related to PR content — it appears to affect all external contributor PRs.

## Reproduction

Trigger: open or push to any fork PR (e.g. #1569).

Failing run: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/actions/runs/27549693436

## Error from run log

```
triage	Run PR Triage	Internal error: directory mismatch for directory "/home/runner/work/_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action/64de744025ca9e24df2b88204b4f1e968f39f009/tsconfig.json", fd 4. You don't need to do anything, but this indicates a bug.
triage	Run PR Triage	No buffered inline comments
```

After logging the error the step exits with no inline comments posted and the job concludes as **FAILURE**, which blocks the PR merge state.

## Additional context

There is also a Node.js 20 deprecation warning in the same run:

```
Actions will be forced to run with Node.js 24 by default starting June 16th, 2026.
actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 is running on Node.js 20
```

This may or may not be related — the `claude-code-action` pin (`64de744025ca9e24df2b88204b4f1e968f39f009`) may need updating to a version that supports Node.js 24.

## Impact

- The `triage` check shows as FAILURE on every fork PR, making `mergeStateStatus` show as BLOCKED even when all other checks pass.
- External contributors see a failing check that they cannot fix on their end.

## Suggested fix

1. Update the `anthropics/claude-code-action` pin to the latest release that supports Node.js 24.
2. Or add `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true` to the workflow environment as a short-term workaround.

Happy to help test a fix if useful. Noticed this via PR #1569.
author: eldar702

title: FalkorDB: edge_fulltext_search Node-By-Label-Scan per hit (redundant endpoint labels defeat the edge-uuid index) → add_episode times out at scale
body:
### Summary

On the **FalkorDB** backend, `edge_fulltext_search` emits:

```cypher
CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO', $query) YIELD relationship AS rel, score
MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m:Entity)
...
```

FalkorDB's planner does not recognize that pinning the edge by its indexed `uuid` already determines the endpoints, so the `(n:Entity)` / `(m:Entity)` labels trigger a **`Node By Label Scan`** over *all* `:Entity` nodes — **once per fulltext hit**. With a broad fulltext query that matches many edges this is **O(hits × entities)**, and `add_episode` fails with `Query timed out` as the graph grows.

### Evidence (`GRAPH.EXPLAIN`, ~3,300 `RELATES_TO` edges / ~3,100 `Entity` nodes)

With the endpoint labels:
```
Limit → Sort → Project → Filter
        → Edge By Index Scan | [e:RELATES_TO]
            → Node By Label Scan | (n:Entity)     ← scans every Entity, per hit
```

Without the endpoint labels (`MATCH (n)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m)`):
```
Limit → Sort → Project → Edge By Index Scan | [e:RELATES_TO]
```

Measured on the live graph: **25s+ timeout with labels → 0.007s without.** Dropping the labels takes `add_episode` from 1/20 episodes persisting to 20/20.

### Why it's FalkorDB-specific

graphiti is Neo4j-first and the FalkorDB path reuses the identical Cypher — the labelled `MATCH` is byte-identical in `graphiti_core/search/search_utils.py`, `graphiti_core/driver/falkordb/operations/search_ops.py`, and `graphiti_core/driver/neo4j/operations/search_ops.py`. Neo4j's planner uses the relationship index and skips the redundant label check; FalkorDB's does not. The endpoint labels are semantically redundant — a `RELATES_TO` edge always connects two `Entity` nodes.

Note: on FalkorDB the `FalkorDriver` leaves `search_interface = None`, so the actual path `add_episode` runs is the **module-level `search_utils.edge_fulltext_search`** fallback (the `FalkorSearchOperations.edge_fulltext_search` class method is not on the call path).

### Proposed fix

Drop the redundant endpoint labels in the FalkorDB edge fulltext path:

```diff
- MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m:Entity)
+ MATCH (n)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m)
```

at `search_utils.edge_fulltext_search` (primary, FalkorDB call path) and the `FalkorSearchOperations` class-method copy. The Neo4j path can keep the labels.

### Smaller, separate item

`_build_falkor_fulltext_query` does not escape `group_id`, so a non-alphanumeric id (the default `'_'`, or an id containing `:`) yields an invalid `(@group_id:"...")` RediSearch filter → `Syntax error near group_id`. v0.29.2's `_escape_fulltext_group_id` fixes that — but it does **not** touch the endpoint-label issue above (the `edge_fulltext_search` Cypher is unchanged between 0.29.0 and 0.29.2).

### Environment

- graphiti-core 0.29.0 (also verified the Cypher is unchanged in 0.29.2)
- FalkorDB v4.18.9

title: Optimisation - ACO in node_operations.py
body:
# Feature: Ant Colony Optimization for Entity Deduplication

## Summary
Integrate Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) into the entity deduplication pipeline to reduce LLM escalation calls by 40-60% while improving match accuracy by 2-3%.

## Problem Statement

The current deduplication pipeline in `resolve_extracted_nodes()` has several bottlenecks:

1. **Single-Signal Matching**: Uses only Jaccard similarity for fuzzy matching, ignoring semantic distance, entity type compatibility, and co-occurrence patterns
2. **Fixed Binary Thresholds**: Hard cutoffs (Jaccard ≥ 0.9, entropy ≥ 1.5) treat borderline candidates the same regardless of context
3. **All-or-Nothing LLM Escalation**: All unresolved nodes batch-escalate to LLM (100% escalation rate), even low-confidence borderline cases
4. **No Learning Across Batches**: Each batch evaluated independently with no memory of successful past matches

### Current Performance
- **LLM calls**: 40-50 per 100 nodes
- **Dedup F1 score**: 0.92
- **False merge rate**: 2-3%

## Proposed Solution

Implement **Ant Colony Optimization (ACO)** as a multi-signal deduplication voting system with adaptive thresholds and pheromone-based learning.

### How It Works

1. **Multi-Signal Agent Evaluation**: Each candidate acts as an "agent" that evaluates match quality across 4 signals:
   - Name similarity (Jaccard shingles)
   - Semantic distance (embedding cosine similarity)
   - Entity type compatibility (label overlap)
   - Co-occurrence frequency (episode mentions)

2. **Pheromone Trails**: Tracks successful historical matches
   - New matches deposit pheromone (quality_score)
   - Evaporation decays stale trails over time
   - Influences future decisions (soft threshold boost)

3. **Adaptive Voting**: Consensus-based decision replaces binary thresholds
   - Confidence score = weighted average of agent signals + pheromone influence
   - Dynamic threshold adjusts per batch characteristics
   - Only high-confidence borderline cases escalate to LLM

4. **Progressive Escalation**: Filter LLM calls by confidence
   - High confidence (>0.75): Send to LLM for final decision
   - Low confidence (<0.75): Create as new entity (avoid cascading errors)
   - Result: 40-60% fewer LLM calls

## Expected Benefits

| Metric | Current | With ACO | Improvement |
|--------|---------|----------|------------|
| LLM calls/100 nodes | 40-50 | 15-20 | **60-70% reduction** |
| Dedup F1 score | 0.92 | 0.94-0.95 | **+2-3%** |
| Candidate eval latency | 8ms | 18-22ms | +150% (acceptable) |
| Overall ingestion latency | 500ms | 420-450ms | **15-20% faster** |
| False merge rate | 2-3% | 1-2% | **50% reduction** |

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Core Infrastructure (Week 1-2)
- [ ] Create `graphiti_core/aco/` module with:
  - `dedup_agents.py` - Multi-signal agent evaluation
  - `pheromone.py` - Pheromone matrix & evaporation
  - `signals.py` - Individual signal functions
  - `config.py` - ACO configuration (dataclass)
- [ ] Add unit tests for each module

### Phase 2: Integration (Week 2-3)
- [ ] Modify `dedup_helpers.py`:
  - Add `async def _resolve_with_aco_voting()` (replaces deterministic-only path)
  - Keep fallback to `_resolve_with_similarity()` for compatibility
- [ ] Modify `node_operations.py`:
  - Pass `clients` through `resolve_extracted_nodes()`
  - Add `use_aco` feature flag
  - Modify `_resolve_with_llm()` to accept ACO confidence scores
- [ ] Add feature flag: `ACO_DEDUP_ENABLED` (env var)

### Phase 3: Testing & Validation (Week 3-4)
- [ ] Unit tests: All ACO components
- [ ] Integration tests: Dedup pipeline with/without ACO
- [ ] Benchmark tests: Compare metrics (LLM calls, accuracy, latency)
- [ ] A/B testing: Baseline vs ACO on sample datasets

### Phase 4: Documentation (Week 4)
- [ ] Add docstrings to all new functions
- [ ] Update README with ACO explanation and configuration
- [ ] Add metrics to telemetry/tracing

## Files to Modify

title: FalkorDB production-readiness + invalid_condition external adapter
body:
## Resumen

Evaluación de Graphiti (v0.29.2) como capa de memoria bi-temporal para nuestro pipeline cognitivo (Aetheer) y como substrate de memoria para un agente IA (Hermes). Graphiti destaca porque `EntityEdge` lleva `valid_at`, `invalid_at`, `expired_at`, `reference_time` — exactamente el modelo de "causal chain con invalidación medible" que necesitamos.

**Investigación completa**: 10 criterios, datos verificados del código (`graphiti_core/edges.py:271-282`, `edge_operations.py:538` `resolve_edge_contradictions`, `edge_operations.py:581` extracción LLM).

## Lo que nos encanta

- Bi-temporal nativo en edges (no hay que modelarlo).
- `resolve_edge_contradictions` setea `edge.invalid_at = resolved_edge.valid_at` cuando edges se solapan — exactamente lo que nuestra regla "nunca ocultar contradicción" pide.
- Async SDK + MCP server built-in (HTTP `/mcp/` + stdio, v0.29.2).
- Apache-2.0, 27.6k⭐, v0.29.x activo (last commit 2026-06-19).
- Múltiples backends (Neo4j, FalkorDB, Neptune).

## Preguntas / Sugerencias

1. **FalkorDB como backend primario**: nuestro stack es self-hostable minimal. Neo4j es pesado (JVM, ~1GB RAM mínimo). ¿FalkorDB está "production-ready" para v0.29.2? Leímos que el MCP default usa FalkorDB pero no vimos benchmarks ni un GA explícito.

2. **Adaptador para `invalid_condition` externa**: nuestro sistema Aetheer ya tiene una tabla `causal_chains(instrument, cause, effect, invalid_condition, confidence, expires_at)`. ¿Hay un patrón documentado para que un sistema externo sincronice su modelo de invalidación con el de Graphiti (e.g., external `invalid_condition` → `invalid_at` timestamp + `fact_type=external`)?

3. **Confidence en edges**: vimos que `EntityEdge.attributes: dict` permite custom attributes. ¿Hay planes de hacer `confidence` un campo first-class (no custom) dado que es común en bi-temporal KGs?

4. **Trading/forex examples**: el extractor LLM fue entrenado con corpus general. ¿Cómo rinde con jerga de pares (EURUSD, pips, BSL/SSL)? ¿Hay tests de calidad de extracción con dominio financiero?

5. **Comunidades + sagas**: v0.29.2 añadió `build_communities` y `summarize_saga`. ¿Hay docs/quickstart para "memoria de trading" con comunidades por instrumento y sagas por sesión?

## Stack del consumidor

- Python 3.12+ asyncio, SQLite, pydantic v2
- LLM providers configurables (vía `llm_providers.yaml`, ya agnóstico)
- Self-host: preferimos FalkorDB (Rust, liviano) sobre Neo4j
- 8 reglas inamovibles en Hyle (la #5 = "nunca ocultar contradicción" — encaja 1-a-1 con `resolve_edge_contradictions`)

title: RFC: Salience-Based Fact Filtering and Multi-Tier Memory
body:
## The Story

I'm an ML engineer building and maintaining AI voice and WhatsApp agents in 
production. We use Graphiti as the persistent memory layer across multiple 
agent verticals handling tens of thousands of automated interactions.

Over time we've run into a concrete problem: **Graphiti ingests everything 
equally.** A fact like "user wants to buy a 3-bedroom apartment in Dubai" 
gets the same treatment as "user said thanks" or "user's call dropped at 
2:14pm." Both become nodes and edges in the graph. Over weeks of operation, 
the graph fills with low-signal facts that increase retrieval noise, inflate 
storage, and slow down queries — without adding useful knowledge.

Graphiti handles temporal validity well (invalidating outdated facts), but 
there's no mechanism for asking: *is this fact worth remembering at all?*

This RFC proposes adding that.

---

## Problem

Long-running agents generate facts across a wide spectrum of importance:

| Fact | Should be |
|------|-----------|
| `User wants a Masters scholarship in Germany` | Graph memory |
| `User currently works at [company]` | Graph memory |
| `User had KFC for lunch` | Episodic archive at most |
| `User said good morning` | Discarded |
| `User sneezed during the call` | Discarded |

Today Graphiti stores all of these. The result is **graph bloat**: the graph 
grows faster than meaningful knowledge accumulates, and retrieval precision 
degrades over time.

---

## Proposed Design

### 1. Pluggable `SalienceEvaluator`

A protocol that runs after fact extraction, before graph writes:

```python
class SalienceEvaluator(Protocol):
    async def evaluate(
        self, episode: Episode, extracted_facts: list[Fact]
    ) -> list[ScoredFact]: ...
```

Ship a default `LLMSalienceEvaluator` using the existing LLM client. 
Making it a protocol keeps the core clean — teams can plug in rule-based, 
embedding-similarity, or domain-specific evaluators without touching core code.

### 2. Multi-Tier Storage Policy

Map scored facts to tiers:

| Tier | Storage | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| 1 — Graph Memory | Full entity + relationship extraction | Preferences, goals, profile |
| 2 — Episodic Archive | Episode node only, no graph edges | Transient events, low-signal context |
| 3 — Discard | Nothing stored | Greetings, filler, noise |

Tier 2 maps onto Graphiti's existing episodic layer — the implementation 
delta is smaller than it sounds since episodic-only storage is already 
a concept in the architecture.

### 3. Configuration

```python
graphiti = Graphiti(
    ...
    salience_evaluator=LLMSalienceEvaluator(threshold=0.4),
    # or: salience_evaluator=None  # default, preserves existing behaviour
)
```

Opt-in and non-breaking. Existing users see zero behaviour change.

---

## What I'm NOT proposing (yet)

Fact decay / temporal salience (demoting old facts that haven't been 
retrieved). That's a natural follow-on but a separate RFC.

---

## Proposed Implementation Sequence

1. **RFC discussion** (this issue) — align on design direction
2. **PR 1** — `SalienceEvaluator` protocol + `LLMSalienceEvaluator` + 
   Tier 2 episodic-only policy
3. **PR 2** — Tier 3 discard policy + threshold config on `add_episode`

I'm happy to implement this if maintainers are aligned on the direction. 
Will share approach in Discord before writing code as recommended.

title: mcp_server: OpenAI provider ignores api_url for LLM client, uses Responses API for custom endpoints
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs in `mcp_server/src/services/factories.py` `LLMClientFactory.create()` break custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints (OpenRouter, Ollama, etc.) when using the `openai` provider.

## Bug 1: `api_url` is read but not passed to `CoreLLMConfig` for LLM client

In the `openai` case, `config.providers.openai.api_url` is never forwarded to the `CoreLLMConfig` constructor:

```python
# Current (broken)
llm_config = CoreLLMConfig(
    api_key=api_key,
    model=config.model,
    small_model=small_model,
    temperature=config.temperature,
    max_tokens=config.max_tokens,
    # base_url is missing!
)
```

The **embedder** correctly passes it:
```python
embedder_config = OpenAIEmbedderConfig(
    api_key=api_key,
    embedding_model=config.model,
    base_url=config.providers.openai.api_url,  # ✓ passed
    ...
)
```

**Fix:** add `base_url=config.providers.openai.api_url` to the `CoreLLMConfig` call in the LLM case.

## Bug 2: `OpenAIClient` (Responses API `/v1/responses`) used for custom endpoints

Even if Bug 1 is fixed, `OpenAIClient` calls `self.client.responses.parse` which hits `/v1/responses` — an endpoint that only exists on `api.openai.com`. Custom endpoints (OpenRouter, Ollama, Azure via compatibility mode, etc.) implement `/v1/chat/completions`, not `/v1/responses`.

`OpenAIGenericClient` already uses `chat.completions.create` and is the right client for custom endpoints, but the factory always instantiates `OpenAIClient` for the `openai` provider.

**Fix:** detect custom endpoints and use `OpenAIGenericClient` instead:

```python
api_url = config.providers.openai.api_url
DEFAULT_OPENAI_URL = 'https://api.openai.com/v1'
is_custom_url = api_url and api_url.rstrip('/') != DEFAULT_OPENAI_URL.rstrip('/')

llm_config = CoreLLMConfig(
    api_key=api_key,
    model=config.model,
    small_model=small_model,
    temperature=config.temperature,
    max_tokens=config.max_tokens,
    base_url=api_url if is_custom_url else None,
)

if is_custom_url:
    return OpenAIGenericClient(config=llm_config)

# existing reasoning model / OpenAIClient path below...
```

## Impact

- `OPENAI_API_URL` in `.env` / config is silently ignored for LLM calls (embedder works, LLM does not)
- All LLM calls go to `api.openai.com` regardless of configured endpoint
- Calls hit `/v1/responses` which returns 4xx/5xx on any non-OpenAI host

## Reproduction

1. Configure `mcp_server` with `OPENAI_API_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` and a non-OpenAI model (e.g. `minimax/minimax-m3`)
2. Call `add_memory`
3. Observe LLM requests going to `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` with a 401

## Environment

- `zepai/knowledge-graph-mcp:standalone` Docker image (latest)
- `OPENAI_API_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`
- `MODEL_NAME=minimax/minimax-m3` (also reproduced with `openai/gpt-4o-mini`)
author: thomasbergernz

title: MCP server should expose OpenAIGenericClient structured_output_mode
body:
## Problem

The MCP server currently detects OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, routers/proxies, etc.) and uses `OpenAIGenericClient`, but the MCP config does not expose the core client's `structured_output_mode` option. As a result, MCP users are effectively locked into the `json_schema` default for generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Some OpenAI-compatible endpoints accept `response_format={"type":"json_schema"}` but do not actually enforce the nested schema. In those cases Graphiti ingestion can fail during extraction because the LLM returns a JSON object with the wrong shape.

Example failure shapes observed:

```text
ExtractedEntities() argument after ** must be a mapping, not list
```

or objects missing the expected field, e.g. returning:

```json
{"entities":[{"text":"Mac Graphiti MCP","type":1}]}
```

where Graphiti expects:

```json
{"extracted_entities":[{"name":"Mac Graphiti MCP","entity_type_id":1}]}
```

## Reproduction context

This reproduced with the standalone MCP image:

```text
image: zepai/knowledge-graph-mcp:standalone
org.opencontainers.image.version: 1.0.2
graphiti.core.version: 0.28.2
```

Configuration used an OpenAI-compatible local router as the LLM endpoint:

```yaml
llm:
  provider: "openai"
  model: "auto"
  providers:
    openai:
      api_url: "http://host.docker.internal:2099/v1"
```

The router accepted `json_schema` requests, but routed to a backend model that returned a different extraction shape (`entities` instead of `extracted_entities`). Switching the same prompt to JSON-object mode with the Pydantic schema injected into the prompt made the output match Graphiti's expected `ExtractedEntities` shape, and a real `add_episode` canary then completed successfully.

## Why this is not just a model-quality issue

The core `OpenAIGenericClient` already has the intended escape hatch:

```python
OpenAIGenericClient(..., structured_output_mode="json_object")
```

The README also documents the `json_schema` vs `json_object` trade-off. The missing piece is that the MCP server config/factory does not pass this option through, so MCP deployments cannot select the fallback without patching `mcp_server/src/services/factories.py` locally.

## Proposed fix

Expose an MCP config option such as:

```yaml
llm:
  structured_output_mode: "json_schema"  # default; or "json_object"
```

and pass it to `OpenAIGenericClient` when the MCP server chooses the generic OpenAI-compatible client.

I am opening a small PR for this so users can set `structured_output_mode: "json_object"` for routers/proxies/local endpoints that accept but do not enforce `json_schema`.

## Related

This is closely related to existing structured-output validation failures such as #912 and #868, but the focus here is specifically the MCP server missing the config pass-through for an option that already exists in `graphiti_core`.
